sources.title: Coimbra Research Group - About
sources.text: Search this site Embedded Files Coimbra Research Group About Us We are a multidisciplinary research group headed by Professor Carlos F. M. Coimbra . Prof. Coimbra received his Ph.D. in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from the University of California Irvine ( UCI ) after graduating in both Mechanical Engineering and Physics from the University of Brasilia, and receiving a Masters of Science degree in Applied Thermodynamics/Energy from the IST/University of Lisbon. Prof. Coimbra is also associated with the Center for Energy Research (CER), which is one of the largest Organized Research Units (ORUs) at UCSD . Prof. Coimbra has published over 100 journal papers on various topics related to solar energy, heat and mass transfer, stochastic forecasting, energy meteorology, atmospheric physics, unsteady multiphase flows, and nonlinear dynamics. He is the co-author (with Prof. Anthony F. Mills from UCLA ) of a popular series of textbooks on Heat and Mass Transfer, a Fellow of the American Society of Mechanical Engineers ( ASME ), and a life member of the American Geophysical Union ( AGU ). sources.text: Faculty Profiles Back to Faculty Profiles Carlos Coimbra Professor, MAE Center for Energy Research Heat and mass transfer, stochastic modeling and forecasting, variable order methods, longwave and shortwave radiation, cloud physics; concentrated solar power. Interests for Coimbra’s research group include: heat and mass transfer; energy meteorology; atmospheric radiation; cloud physics; optical properties; multiphase flows; real-time forecasting; stochastic learning and variable order methods. Visit the Carlos Coimbra research page at UC San Diego . Capsule Bio: Professor Coimbra received his Ph.D. in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from the University of California, Irvine. He joined the Jacobs School of Engineering at UC San Diego in July of 2011, and is now a Co-Director of the UCSD Center for Excellence in Renewable Resource Integration (CERRI) and the Chairman of the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering.
